text: Add impression-time request-context features tab, hourmin, and weekday to the existing factorization-machine scorer while keeping architecture, pointwise BCE training, split, and evaluation fixed.
rationale: Training-only screening measured a positive primary lift of 0.00221 for this feature group across all four days, although daily variability was larger than the mean lift. The latest model has GAUC 0.6499 and nDCG@5 0.5272, leaving room for context-sensitive ordering improvements.
exact_ablation: Compare parent experiment 1 using user_id and video_id alone against the same factorization-machine scorer augmented only with tab, hourmin, and weekday.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.001 to 0.003, especially for context-dependent users; uncertainty is high because the screening daily standard deviation was 0.00580.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.001 to 0.004, with the largest opportunity in weak context slices such as tab 8 and tab 5.

text: Replace the factorization-machine interaction dimension of 16 with dimension 8, leaving the feature set, pointwise BCE objective, optimizer, and all data handling unchanged.
rationale: The parent reaches GAUC 0.6499 and nDCG@5 0.5272, but its interaction model may overfit sparse user-item pairs. A smaller embedding provides a materially distinct capacity ablation and is computationally cheaper, which may improve generalization on rare items where the parent has primary 0.3859.
exact_ablation: Compare interaction dimension 16 in parent experiment 1 with interaction dimension 8; change no other model or training setting.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.002 if capacity reduction improves sparse-pair generalization; it could be neutral or slightly negative.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.003 through less noisy top-five scores for rare and medium-frequency items.

text: Replace pointwise BCE training with within-user pairwise BPR training using one positive and one negative impression per eligible user, keeping the factorization-machine scorer and feature set unchanged.
rationale: The official objective is within-user ranking, while the parent uses pointwise BCE and obtains GAUC 0.6499 with nDCG@5 0.5272. The research evidence identifies pairwise objectives as better aligned with ranking, and the zero-positive diagnostic confirms that users without both classes must be excluded from pair construction.
exact_ablation: Keep parent experiment 1's factorization-machine architecture and user/item inputs, but replace only pointwise BCE updates with within-user BPR pairs sampled from users having at least one positive and one negative.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.002 to 0.008 because the loss directly optimizes positive-over-negative ordering within users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.001 to 0.006, with possible gains in top-five placement; sparse users may see unstable estimates.

text: Replace pointwise BCE training with a within-user listwise softmax loss over each user's logged impression group, retaining the parent factorization-machine scorer and current feature inputs.
rationale: The task evaluates within-user GAUC and nDCG@5, whereas the parent optimizes pointwise BCE and scores GAUC 0.6499 and nDCG@5 0.5272. A listwise loss is a distinct ranking-alignment hypothesis, provided groups are bounded or minibatched to avoid unbounded computation.
exact_ablation: Change only the training loss from pointwise BCE to a numerically stable within-user listwise softmax loss; preserve the parent model, features, split, and evaluation.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.001 to 0.006 by emphasizing relative ordering within users rather than marginal classification.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.002 to 0.008 because the loss targets concentration of relevant items near the top; users with one positive may dominate variance.

text: Initialize factorization-machine embeddings with small deterministic Gaussian values instead of zeros, leaving the architecture, pointwise BCE objective, learning rate, and feature set unchanged.
rationale: The parent uses zero-initialized interaction embeddings, yet its interaction term must break symmetry to learn useful pair structure; the achieved GAUC 0.6499 and nDCG@5 0.5272 show useful but potentially underdeveloped interactions. A controlled initialization ablation tests whether the interaction pathway is learning efficiently without adding features.
exact_ablation: Compare parent experiment 1's all-zero embedding initialization with deterministic Gaussian initialization at standard deviation 0.01; change no other code or configuration.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.004 if nonzero initialization accelerates and diversifies interaction learning; optimization variance is a material risk.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.003, with possible degradation if early noisy interactions disturb top-five ordering.

text: Increase the factorization-machine embedding dimension from 16 to 32 while keeping the parent feature set, pointwise BCE loss, optimizer, split, and evaluation protocol fixed.
rationale: The parent already benefits from interaction modeling, reaching GAUC 0.6499 versus a neutral scaffold, while top-five quality remains moderate at nDCG@5 0.5272. More interaction capacity may capture heterogeneous user-item preferences, but the rare-item primary of 0.3859 indicates overfitting and sparsity are important risks.
exact_ablation: Change only the interaction dimension from 16 to 32 in the parent factorization-machine scorer.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.003 on warm pairs, but potentially decline by up to 0.002 overall from sparse-pair overfitting.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.004 if additional capacity improves personalized top-five separation; rare-item nDCG may worsen.

text: Replace Adam-style adaptive updates with plain SGD at a tuned learning rate, leaving the factorization-machine architecture, pointwise BCE loss, feature set, and epoch budget unchanged.
rationale: The parent achieves GAUC 0.6499 but has broad segment variation, including very weak tab 8 and tab 5 top-five results. Optimizer dynamics may be amplifying frequent entities and undertraining sparse interactions; a plain-SGD ablation tests whether more uniform updates improve ranking calibration.
exact_ablation: Replace only the Adam-style parameter updates in parent experiment 1 with minibatch SGD using a fixed tuned learning rate; retain all data, loss, architecture, and stopping rules.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.004 if uniform updates improve within-user ordering, with a meaningful risk of slower or less stable convergence.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.003 if sparse-user and sparse-item scores become less dominated by frequent updates.

text: Add a learned user-by-request-context interaction block for tab, hourmin, and weekday, while retaining the parent user/item interaction scorer and excluding all other feature additions.
rationale: Request-context screening produced a positive primary lift of 0.00221, and several hour slices are substantially weaker than the global parent, such as hour 3 with GAUC 0.5409 and nDCG@5 0.3869. Explicit user-context interactions test personalization of the confirmed available context signal rather than merely adding independent biases.
exact_ablation: Keep parent experiment 1 unchanged except add second-order interactions between the user representation and tab, hourmin, and weekday representations.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.001 to 0.005, concentrated in users whose preferences vary by time or surface.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.002 to 0.007 in weak hour and tab slices, though sparse context combinations may overfit.

text: Use inverse-frequency weighting for training impressions so rare user-item examples receive higher pointwise BCE weight, while keeping the parent scorer, feature set, and objective form unchanged.
rationale: The parent has much weaker item-frequency performance for rare items, with GAUC 0.6000, nDCG@5 0.1717, and primary 0.3859, despite global GAUC 0.6499. Reweighting is a targeted training change intended to reduce frequent-item dominance without introducing unavailable item statistics as inference features.
exact_ablation: Change only BCE example weights to a capped inverse training-frequency weight for the item, with weights computed from training data; retain unweighted inference and all parent architecture settings.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.000 to 0.004 overall and by more on rare items, with possible degradation for warm items from noisier estimates.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.002 to 0.010 for rare and medium-frequency items because their relevant rows receive more optimization attention.

text: Apply gradient clipping by global norm 1.0 during factorization-machine training, leaving the parent architecture, pointwise BCE loss, learning rate, feature set, and split unchanged.
rationale: The parent has a wide score range from -5.99 to 2.68 and highly uneven segment quality, including very low top-five performance in tab 8 and tab 5. Clipping is a single stability ablation that may prevent high-frequency batches from producing disproportionate updates, though it may also suppress useful rare-event gradients.
exact_ablation: Add only global-norm gradient clipping at 1.0 before each parent parameter update.

expected_effect.GAUC: Remain near baseline or increase by 0.000 to 0.002 if unstable updates are harming ordering; excessive clipping could reduce GAUC.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Remain near baseline or increase by 0.000 to 0.003 through more stable top-five scores, with risk of reduced separation.

text: Replace uniform random minibatch sampling with user-balanced minibatches that sample users uniformly and then bounded impression subsets, keeping the parent loss, model, features, and total update budget fixed.
rationale: The official GAUC is positive-count-weighted within-user AUC, while the parent trains on row-level minibatches and produces global GAUC 0.6499. User-balanced sampling tests whether reducing domination by high-volume users improves the task-aligned ordering signal; the zero-positive diagnostic shows that user eligibility must not be inferred from validation labels.
exact_ablation: Change only minibatch construction from row-uniform sampling to uniform eligible-user sampling with a fixed per-user cap; preserve pointwise BCE and all parent model settings.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.001 to 0.005 by giving lower-volume users more influence, with possible loss on the positive-count-weighted aggregate.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.001 to 0.005 if more users receive calibrated top-five rankings; small groups may add variance.

text: Add a bounded, strictly pre-impression user history encoder over prior interactions, while keeping the factorization-machine scorer as the only scored head and leaving all static features unchanged.
rationale: The parent has GAUC 0.6499 and nDCG@5 0.5272 using only current user and item IDs, so it lacks sequential preference information. The research evidence identifies leakage-safe sequential histories as a high-value family; the parent’s weak rare-item and low-context top-five slices suggest prior behavior could help disambiguate candidates, but strict timestamp construction and bounded history are required.
exact_ablation: Keep parent experiment 1 unchanged except concatenate a bounded encoder of the user's most recent pre-impression interaction IDs and labels, constructed separately for each target timestamp without future events.

expected_effect.GAUC: Increase by approximately 0.002 to 0.010 for users with sufficient history, with little or no gain for cold users and a substantial implementation-risk interval.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Increase by approximately 0.002 to 0.010 through better personalized top-five placement, but stale or noisy histories could lower nDCG@5.
